description: The crew's uneasy integration deepens as Seska's Kazon alliance, Vidiian encounters and increasingly difficult ethical choices test whether Voyager can preserve Federation principles far from Federation support.

s02e01.description: Chakotay becomes entangled in a Kazon youth's violent rite of passage while trying to honor both cultures without killing him.

s02e02.description: Harry Kim wakes in an alternate life on Earth where he never joined Voyager and tries to reconstruct how history changed.

s02e03.description: Paris and Neelix are forced to cooperate on an away mission while their rivalry over Kes reaches breaking point.

s02e04.description: An alien telepath incapacitates the crew by manifesting their deepest desires and fears, leaving Kes to resist the attack.

s02e05.description: Chakotay follows symbols linked to his father's traditions and discovers an alien connection to his people's distant past.

s02e06.description: Voyager finds another Caretaker-related entity while Kes's expanding psychic powers are manipulated by an embittered Ocampa mentor.

s02e07.description: Seska and the Kazon raid Voyager for Federation technology, drawing Chakotay into a personal attempt to recover what was stolen.

s02e08.description: Janeway joins an eccentric resistance fighter after Tuvok and B'Elanna are captured by an authoritarian regime.

s02e09.description: B'Elanna revives an automated soldier and is abducted into a war between two machine civilizations seeking the ability to reproduce.

s02e10.description: Janeway reluctantly considers alliances with Kazon factions after repeated attacks challenge Starfleet principles in the Delta Quadrant.

s02e11.description: Paris reaches transwarp velocity and begins undergoing a bizarre biological transformation that soon affects Janeway as well.

s02e12.description: Tuvok mind-melds with a remorseless murderer and finds the man's violence destabilizing his own carefully controlled emotions.

s02e13.description: Voyager encounters a Cardassian missile B'Elanna once reprogrammed, now mistakenly targeting an inhabited Delta Quadrant world.

s02e14.description: A suicidal member of the Q Continuum asks Janeway for asylum and the right to die, forcing Q to defend immortality itself.

s02e15.description: The Doctor creates a holographic body for a Vidiian woman and forms an attachment while treating her fatal disease.

s02e16.description: Paris's apparent departure becomes part of a plan to expose a Kazon informant, with Neelix unexpectedly central to uncovering the spy.

s02e17.description: A spatial anomaly duplicates Voyager, leaving two damaged crews occupying the same coordinates while the Vidiians close in.

s02e18.description: Tuvok is stranded with frightened alien children whose apparent abandonment hides an unsettling truth about their society.

s02e19.description: Voyager discovers colonists trapped in a shared virtual reality ruled by a sadistic embodiment of fear.

s02e20.description: A transporter accident fuses Tuvok and Neelix into a single new person who develops his own identity and refuses separation.

s02e21.description: Janeway and Chakotay are left behind on a planet after contracting an incurable illness while Voyager seeks help from the Vidiians.

s02e22.description: Seska lures Voyager into a Kazon trap that ends with the ship captured and its crew abandoned on a hostile planet.
